extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent applicants/owners, patent attorneys and agents who prosecute before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards in the MPEP governing powers of attorney, acting in a representative capacity, signature and certification requirements, revocation and withdrawal procedures, and assignee rights for U.S. patent applications and proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney should be signed by assignee of entire interest when one exists
rubrics_metrics.description: While a power of attorney may be signed by the inventor(s), the power of attorney should be signed by the assignee of the entire interest where one exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Otherwise the assignee may be paying the bill while the inventor provides the POA, creating questions about who is the practitioner’s client; relationships may deteriorate and inventors may attempt to control prosecution. A power of attorney by the assignee of the entire interest revokes prior powers if the assignee establishes their right to take action as provided in pre‑AIA 37 CFR 3.71 and pre‑AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b). See MPEP §324.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify change in power of attorney in continuing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a continuation or divisional with a copy of a declaration from the parent under pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.63(d), applicants are required to identify in the continuing/divisional any change in power of attorney that occurred after filing the parent application (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.63(d)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested practice: submit a copy of the most recent power of attorney from the parent application in the continuing/divisional to ensure the Office recognizes the correct power of attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of POA forms for applications filed before September 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/80 or PTO/SB/81 should be used for powers of attorney in applications filed before September 16, 2012; Form PTO/SB/81A may be used in a patent that issued from an application filed before that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office does not recommend use of a combined declaration and power of attorney document and no longer provides such a combined form on the USPTO website. All Office POA forms include revocation language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for practitioner-filed papers
rubrics_metrics.description: For all documents filed in the Office (patent, trademark, non‑patent matters) except correspondence required to be signed by the applicant/party, each piece of correspondence filed by a practitioner must bear a signature personally signed or inserted by such practitioner in compliance with §1.4(d) or §2.193(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 11.18(a) which emphasizes every paper filed by a practitioner must be personally signed by the practitioner, except those required to be signed by the applicant/party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of truthfulness and criminal penalties (37 CFR 11.18(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: By presenting any paper to the Office, the presenter certifies that all statements made therein of the party’s own knowledge are true, and those made on information and belief are believed to be true; false statements may incur penalties under 18 U.S.C. 1001 and other criminal statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations may jeopardize the probative value of the paper; the certification is analogous to the declaration clause of 37 CFR 1.68 and Rule 11(b) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. See MPEP §410.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications about inquiry and meritoriousness (37 CFR 11.18(b)(2)(i–iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: By presenting a paper, to the best of the party’s knowledge, information and belief formed after a reasonable inquiry, the party certifies: (i) paper is not for an improper purpose; (ii) legal contentions are warranted by existing law or nonfrivolous argument for change; (iii) factual allegations have evidentiary support or are likely to after reasonable opportunity; (iv) denials of factual contentions are warranted on the evidence or reasonably based on lack of information or belief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of these certifications may result in the sanctions described in 37 CFR 11.18(c). The certifications apply to all papers including allegations of improper conduct by practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available for violations of 37 CFR 11.18(b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of paragraphs (b)(2)(i)–(iv) are, after notice and opportunity to respond, subject to sanctions as deemed appropriate by the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions may include striking the offending paper; referring practitioner conduct to OED Director; precluding submission of papers or contesting issues; affecting weight given to the paper; terminating proceedings. Additionally 37 CFR 11.18(d) provides disciplinary action may be taken against practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting in a representative capacity constitutes representation and requires registration info (37 CFR 1.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent practitioner acts in a representative capacity by appearing in person or signing a paper, their appearance or signature represents they are authorized to represent the particular party; the practitioner must set forth registration number, name, and signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further proof of authority to act may be required. Acceptance of papers by registered attorneys/agents upon representation they are authorized is for facilitating replies and obviating need to file POAs when law firm composition changes. Design practitioners acting in representative capacity may only do so in design matters (see MPEP §1502.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner must represent all identified applicants when acting in representative capacity (post‑Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent practitioner acts in a representative capacity by filing a paper in an application filed on or after September 16, 2012, they must be submitting the paper on behalf of all parties identified as the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner cannot file papers on behalf of only some applicants or assignees (e.g., one joint inventor cannot file to the exclusion of the other joint inventors). Powers of attorney by fewer than all applicants/owners are not accepted unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.36(a) or 1.183 is granted that results in more than one attorney/agent signing correspondence. Acting in representative capacity under 1.34 is not a means to prosecute for only some applicant parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on documents signable by a representative-capacity practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as noted, a person acting in a representative capacity may not sign: (A) a power of attorney (37 CFR 1.32), (B) a document granting access to an application, (C) a change of correspondence address, (D) a terminal disclaimer (37 CFR 1.321(b)(1)), or (E) a request for express abandonment without filing a continuing application (37 CFR 1.138(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions for applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012: a representative may sign a document granting access or a change of correspondence address if (1) a power of attorney has not been appointed under 37 CFR 1.32(b) and (2) the practitioner was named in the application transmittal papers (see 1.14(c)/1.33(a) rules; analogous pre‑AIA rules for earlier applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of power of attorney effective upon receipt by the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocation of a power of attorney becomes effective on the date the revocation is RECEIVED in the Office (not on the date of acceptance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon revocation, appropriate notification is sent by the Office. During an interference or derivation proceeding, any power of attorney or revocation should be forwarded to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board for consideration. All Office POA forms include revocation language and will revoke any existing POA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant revocation rules for applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 (37 CFR 1.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney pursuant to §1.32(b) may be revoked at any stage by the applicant or patent owner. A power of attorney to practitioners associated with a Customer Number is treated as a request to revoke any prior POAs. Fewer than all applicants/owners may revoke only upon showing sufficient cause and payment of petition fee (§1.17(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent practitioner will be notified of revocation; notice mailed to the correspondence address in effect before revocation. An assignment alone does not automatically revoke a prior POA, but an assignee may become applicant under 1.46(c) and revoke previous POAs and grant a new POA per §1.32(b). See MPEP §402.02(a) for appointment of new POA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most recently filed power of attorney controls
rubrics_metrics.description: When an original POA is filed and a subsequent POA is filed (even if not expressly revoking prior POAs), the subsequently filed POA will be treated as a revocation of the original; the most recently filed POA will control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, if a second POA gives power to practitioners associated with a different Customer Number, the second replaces the first and the first Customer Number is automatically revoked. If an assignee later takes action and files a new POA, the original is revoked and replaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant revocation rules for applications filed before Sept 16, 2012 (pre‑AIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre‑Sept.16,2012 applications, a power of attorney may be revoked at any stage by an applicant, assignee of the entire interest, or owner of the entire interest of a patent (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 1.36). Fewer than all applicants or fewer than all assignees may revoke only upon showing sufficient cause and payment of petition fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/81 may be used to revoke a POA in pre‑AIA applications. Addition of an inventor under §1.48 who does not provide a POA consistent with the original may result in loss of that POA upon grant of the §1.48 request. Nonsigning inventors joining via pre‑AIA §1.63 cannot revoke or grant POA without agreement of the pre‑AIA §1.47 applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of adding inventors or nonsigning inventors on POA
rubrics_metrics.description: If the power of attorney was granted by originally named inventive entity and an added inventor under §1.48 does not provide a POA consistent with the original, the addition results in loss of that POA upon grant of the §1.48 request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nonsigning inventor or legal representative may subsequently join by submitting an oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63, but submission by a nonsigning inventor in an application filed under 1.43/1.45/1.46 will not permit the nonsigning inventor to revoke or grant a POA (37 CFR 1.64(f)). See MPEP §402.02(a)/(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney or agent may withdraw only upon application and approval (37 CFR 1.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered patent attorney or agent given a POA pursuant to §1.32(b) may withdraw as attorney or agent of record upon application to and approval by the Director; the applicant/patent owner will be notified of the withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where power is given to practitioners associated with a Customer Number, a request to delete all associated practitioners may not be granted if an application has an Office action to which a reply is due and insufficient time remains to file a reply. See §41.5 for PTAB proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory and permissive grounds for withdrawal (37 CFR 11.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory withdrawal: practitioner shall not represent or must withdraw if representation will result in violation of Rules of Professional Conduct or other law; practitioner’s physical/mental condition materially impairs ability; practitioner is discharged. Permissive withdrawal: practitioner may withdraw if withdrawal can be accomplished without material adverse effect; client persists in criminal/fraudulent course; client used services to perpetrate crime/fraud; client insists on repugnant action; client fails to fulfill obligation after warning; representation imposes unreasonable financial burden or is rendered unreasonably difficult; other good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When termination requires tribunal notice/permission, practitioner must comply. For withdrawal based on client nonpayment or difficulty, be mindful of confidentiality rules (37 CFR 11.106); prefer stating reasons as “irreconcilable differences” and submit supporting evidence as proprietary material under MPEP §724.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner duties on termination of representation (37 CFR 11.116(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon termination, a practitioner shall take steps reasonably practicable to protect client’s interests: give reasonable notice, allow time to employ other counsel, surrender papers/property client is entitled to, and refund any advance payment not earned or incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner may retain papers relating to the client to extent permitted by other law. Where withdrawal is ordered by tribunal, practitioner shall continue representation notwithstanding good cause until ordered otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal notice formality and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Each attorney of record must sign the notice of withdrawal, or the notice must clearly indicate one attorney signing on behalf of another; a withdrawal of another attorney/agent of record without also withdrawing the signing attorney is a revocation, not a withdrawal. Withdrawal is effective when approved rather than when received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing a request to withdraw, the patent attorney/agent should briefly state reasons for withdrawal so the Office can determine whether to grant it. Use PTO/SB/83 or PTO/AIA/83 forms (or web ePetition) which include a section to certify completion of activities necessary for withdrawal to be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will not grant withdrawal requests for practitioners acting in representative capacity (37 CFR 1.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not approve requests from practitioners to withdraw from applications where the requesting practitioner is acting, or has acted, in a representative capacity pursuant to 37 CFR 1.34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such practitioners remain responsible for correspondence they filed while acting in representative capacity and remain responsible for noncompliance with 37 CFR 1.56 and 37 CFR 11.18. In these situations there is no need for permission to withdraw as the practitioner is responsible for prior filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of correspondence address when withdrawing
rubrics_metrics.description: If withdrawal will change the correspondence address, withdrawing practitioner(s) must request that the Office direct all future correspondence to (i) the first named inventor or assignee properly made of record (for pre‑Sept 16, 2012 apps), or (ii) the applicant (for apps filed on or after Sept 16, 2012), or (iii) the assignee of record for issued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners may specify either the correspondence address of, or the address associated with the Customer Number of, any appropriate party as specified. Withdrawing practitioners cannot change the correspondence address to the Customer Number of another law firm or any other address except those noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for withdrawal/revocation requests relative to reply deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request to withdraw/for revocation is filed prior to the expiration date of a time period for reply (or expiration date obtainable by petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.136), the Office will review the request and render a decision even if the decision is after the stated reply period; requests filed after expiration will be placed in the file but not treated on their merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only exception where a revocation and POA accompanied with a petition to revive may be treated differently. Requests filed after a patent has issued will be placed in the file but generally not treated on merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee revocation/grant requirements for apps filed on/after Sept 16, 2012
rubrics_metrics.description: In applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, any POA must be signed by the applicant or patent owner. For an assignee to revoke a previously given POA and/or grant a POA, the assignee must become the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§402.02(a), 402.05(a), and MPEP §325 for details on establishing the assignee’s right to take action in post‑AIA applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee revocation and prosecution rights for pre‑Sept 16, 2012 applications (pre‑AIA 37 CFR 3.71/3.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: In pre‑Sept 16, 2012 applications, the assignee of record of the entire interest can revoke the applicant’s POA unless an irrevocable right to prosecute was given. Pre‑AIA 37 CFR 3.71 allows assignees who become of record (per §3.73(b)) to conduct prosecution to the exclusion of inventors or prior assignees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Who may prosecute: (1) a single assignee of the entire right, title and interest of record; or (2) partial assignees together (and/or inventors) who together own the entire right. Becoming of record requires filing a statement under §3.73(b) signed by an authorized party. Form PTO/SB/80 may be used by an assignee to revoke a POA and appoint a new POA; the assignee or newly appointed practitioner must sign the §3.73(b) statement (Form PTO/SB/96 or equivalent).
